about.intro_content: Prof. Si-Yu Wang is a Professor in the Department of Thoracic Oncology at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. He specialises in the multidisciplinary treatment of thoracic neoplasms, with particular expertise in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
about.detailed_content: Prof. Wang's clinical focus spans diagnosis, staging, surgical treatment and multimodality treatment of NSCLC, with particular expertise in the management of N2-stage disease, an area of ongoing debate in thoracic oncology regarding the role of surgery. He currently serves as Principal Investigator on multiple neoadjuvant immunotherapy trials for unresectable stage III NSCLC, including studies combining checkpoint inhibitors with chemotherapy prior to surgery.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Si-Yu Wang

items.question: Does Prof. Si-Yu Wang accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to lung cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Wang's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Wang specialises in the multidisciplinary and multimodality treatment of non-small cell lung cancer, particularly N2-stage and locally advanced disease.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Wang involved in clinical trials for lung cancer?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Wang serves as Principal Investigator on multiple active neoadjuvant immunotherapy trials for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer at SYSUCC.

items.question: What does multimodality treatment for N2 lung cancer involve?
items.answer: Multimodality treatment typically combines chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery, tailored to the individual patient; Prof. Wang's team evaluates each case to determine the appropriate combination and sequencing.
